summary:
[  edit  ]
The Audio Dynamics  CHOP  is designed to control the dynamic range of an audio signal. Dynamic range refers to how loud and quiet the audio is over some period of time. The Operator contains two types of dynamic control: compression and limiting.
It is recommended that you  link  this  CHOP  to an  Info CHOP , so that you can have some visual feedback:  The amount of compression or limiting which is being applied will be displayed in the Info  CHOP .
Compressor
The goal of a compressor is to reduce the amplitude of a signal when it crosses a certain threshold, while introducing little to no harmonic distortion.  The desired threshold is set by the user, and the amount of compression to be applied is determined by the compression ratio.  The attack and release parameters determine how quickly the compression will be applied and released, as incoming signal goes above and below the threshold.
Limiter
The purpose of a limiter is to ensure a signal is within a certain dynamic range, while introducing as little harmonic distortion as possible.  Unlike the compressor, the goal is not to apply a smooth or musical form of dynamic control, but instead to keep the signal within a 'safe' range that is compatible with any CHOPS that are downstream (for example, an Audio Device Out).  This means that the Limiter has a much more abrupt (instant) attack value, which cannot be adjusted by the user.
Input 2:  Side Chain Channels  - Other audio channels coming in can be used to determine the gains that are applied to the audio channels of the first input.
NOTE : This is a useful article for procedurally  mixing audio for games .
See  Audio Filter CHOP ,  Audio Para EQ CHOP ,  Audio Band EQ CHOP ,  Audio Spectrum CHOP
See also:  Envelope CHOP .

parameters.label: Input Gain (dB)
parameters.name: inputgain
parameters.description: This parameter controls the volume of the channel before it reaches the compressor.  If the signal to be compressed is not in a useful dynamic range, this parameter can be used to repair it.

parameters.label: Enable Compressor
parameters.name: enablecompressor
parameters.description: Turns the compressor on or off.

parameters.label: Compression Type
parameters.name: compressiontype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines which compression method to use.

parameters.label: Automatic Gain Control
parameters.name: compagc
parameters.description: This type of compression is suitable for passages of audio which are varying in amplitude over an extended period of time. To apply this type of compression, set the threshold to a value which is near the maximum volume that you want to hear. Apply a large compression ratio (around 1.0), and set the attack and release to high values. As the passage of audio crosses the threshold value, compression will slowly be applied, and if set properly, the signal will be compressed to a constant range. Setting the attack and release too low will cause the output volume to waver too quickly, while high values may cause the compression to be applied too slowly.

parameters.label: Musical Dynamics
parameters.name: compmus
parameters.description: If a passage of vocals or a musical instrument is varying in amplitude and needs to be brought into a uniform dynamic range, try applying this type of compression. Unless a heavy compression sound is desired, it is best to use this effect lightly. Set the threshold into the volume range that you want to compress and apply a low compression ratio. Try different values of attack and release until you achieve a good dynamic balance.

parameters.label: Channel Linking
parameters.name: chanlinkingcomp
parameters.description: ⊞  - As various channels come into the  CHOP , they can either be compressed by an equal amount, or individually.  If they are compressed equally, all of the channels will be evaluated for the highest peak value, and this value will be used to determine the compression amount.

parameters.label: Threshold (dB)
parameters.name: thresholdcompressor
parameters.description: This parameter sets the threshold value which a signal must cross before compression is applied. It uses a decibel scale, where '0 decibels' would be considered the loudest possible signal*, and '-60 decibels' would be nearly inaudible. This is assuming that input signals are normalized to a "-1 to +1" range.

parameters.label: Ratio
parameters.name: ratiocompressor
parameters.description: The ratio is the amount of compression that will be applied to the signal, with respect to how far the signal has gone past the threshold value. A ratio of '0' will apply no compression. A value of '1' will cause a signals amplitude to be held down to the threshold value. With values over '1', the signal will become quieter as it passes the threshold.

parameters.label: Knee
parameters.name: kneecompressor
parameters.description: The knee defines how the  CHOP  will transition into compression as signals approach or cross the threshold. With a knee of '0' (a hard knee), think of the compressor as applying a flat compression response, where:

parameters.label: Attack (msec=10**val)
parameters.name: attackcompressor
parameters.description: The attack will control how quickly the compressor responds when a signal crosses the threshold.  Increasing the attack parameter will cause the compressor to apply compression at a slower and smoother rate. Increasing the parameter too much, will cause compression to be applied too slowly.

parameters.label: Release (msec=10**val)
parameters.name: releasecompressor
parameters.description: The release will control how quickly the compressor responds when a signal drops to a lower level, or goes below the threshold altogether. Just like the attack, higher value will slow down the response, but too high of a value will be too slow.

parameters.label: Output Gain (dB)
parameters.name: gaincompressor
parameters.description: After applying compression, the signal can be reduced with Gain to a lower volume level. To make up the lost volume, this parameter can be increased.

parameters.label: Enable Limiter
parameters.name: enablelimiter
parameters.description: Turns the limiter on or off.

parameters.label: Channel Linking
parameters.name: chanlinkinglim
parameters.description: ⊞  - Same as compressor.

parameters.label: Threshold (dB)
parameters.name: thresholdlimiter
parameters.description: This is the threshold value which a signal must cross before limiting is applied. Usually, this value should be left at '0' decibels. Just like the compressor, a value of '0' decibels is considered to be the loudest possible signal.

parameters.label: From the perspective of digital audio, a signal level which varies between "+1 <
parameters.description: > -1" is at a volume level of "0" decibels, because it is not possible for a digital system to respresent any values larger than "+1 <-> -1".  Instead, they will simply be clipped as they proceed to the output device. The limiter allows you to stop your audio from being clipped if you exceed this range, and applies a much smoother form of fast compression, which is barely audible.

parameters.label: Release (msec=10**val)
parameters.name: releaselimiter
parameters.description: Although the attack of a limiter is always quick, the release can still be set by the user. This will determine how long the limiter takes to transition out of a limiting situation. Increasing the release will help smooth out the effect of the limiter. Too high of a value may cause the limiter to release too slowly.  For example, after an excessively loud tone burst, the limiter's gain may have been pushed up to an extreme value. This extreme value will take a long time to be fully released.

parameters.label: Knee
parameters.name: kneelimiter
parameters.description: Similar to the compressor, this parameter controls how the  CHOP  will transition into limiting, when a signal becomes louder. A larger knee will mean a smoother transition. See the Knee diagram above.

parameters.label: Dry / Wet Mix
parameters.name: drywet
parameters.description: As this parameter is reduced from 1 (Wet) toward 0 (Dry), it removes the effect of the filter.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: compressor_multiplier
parameters.description: the amount that the compressor reduced the loudness. 1 means no-change. expressed not in dB – linear

parameters.label: limiter_multiplier
parameters.description: the amount that the limiter reduced the loudness. not db – linear

parameters.label: compressor_db
parameters.description: same as above but expressed in decibels

parameters.label: compressor_attack_msec
parameters.description: this is in milliseconds, computed from the parameter which is 1 msec at value 1 and 100,000 msec at value 5 (10**val)

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
